sections.h2: What should a seller know about Manhattan, KS before choosing how to sell?
sections.html:
Manhattan is a college and Army town, and that mix sets the tone for most home sales here. The city is the county seat of Riley County, it reaches into Pottawatomie County, and the 2020 census counted 54,100 people.

Sellers usually weigh three paths: list with an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer. The sections below cover the local facts that change the answer, including water and weather, rental rules, taxes and deed paperwork.

sections.h2: Where is Manhattan and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Manhattan sits in northeastern Kansas where the Big Blue River meets the Kansas River, about 50 miles west of Topeka. The original downtown was built on a broad, flat floodplain, while much of the city around it rolls into the Flint Hills.

Tuttle Creek Reservoir lies about five miles north of town, and the Konza Prairie preserve is to the south. Interstate 70 runs roughly nine miles south of the city, with three exits that feed Manhattan: K-177 at exit 313, McDowell Creek Road at exit 307 and K-18 at exit 303. US-24 crosses the city as Tuttle Creek Boulevard before turning toward Wamego. Manhattan Regional Airport, on K-18 about two miles west of town, has American Eagle service to Chicago O'Hare and Dallas/Fort Worth, and the ATA Bus runs fixed routes inside the city.

Manhattan ZIP codes are 66502, 66503, 66505 and 66506.

sections.h2: How did Manhattan grow into the Little Apple?
sections.html:
Manhattan began in 1855 when New England Free-State settlers arrived under the New England Emigrant Aid Company. A steamer carrying Ohio settlers from the Cincinnati-Manhattan Company ran aground in the Kansas River that June, and the combined town took the name Manhattan on June 29, 1855. It was incorporated on May 30, 1857.

Education drove the next chapter. The Kansas legislature established Kansas State Agricultural College in 1863, and it opened that September as the first public college in Kansas and the first land-grant institution under the Morrill Act. The Kansas Pacific Railroad reached the town in 1866. Every census since 1870 has recorded growth, from 1,173 residents then to 54,100 in 2020.

Kansas State University is the leading employer, with more than 6,000 people working on campus, according to the Manhattan Area Chamber of Commerce. The chamber also points to Fort Riley, the National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility and Caterpillar Work Tools among the larger employers, and the city's 2026 budget book names Kansas State, Fort Riley, USD 383 and Ascension hospital.

The same budget book lists a Manhattan metro labor force of 65,170 with a 3.2% unemployment rate for December 2025.

  • Kansas State University: the campus workforce is the largest in the city.
  • Fort Riley: the 100,656-acre post sits between Manhattan and Junction City and is home to the 1st Infantry Division.
  • Manhattan-Ogden USD 383: the public school district that serves most of the city.
  • Ascension hospital and private employers such as CivicPlus.

sections.h2: What does Manhattan's flood history mean for a house sale?
sections.html:
Flood risk is the first environmental question many Manhattan buyers ask. The city was built at the downstream end of the Big Blue River watershed, and the Big Blue and Kansas Rivers Floodplain Management Plan, sponsored by the Army Corps of Engineers, the State of Kansas, the city and both counties, describes the south and east side of the city as carrying a particular flood risk.

The plan counts 43 flood events between 1904 and 1951. The 1951 flood led to Tuttle Creek Dam, finished in 1962, and the Manhattan Levee System, finished in 1963. The city later raised the levee and replaced original equipment from the 1960s. Residential areas along Casement Road and Marlatt Avenue are named in the plan as part of the studied floodplain, along with the commercial corridor on US-24 in Pottawatomie County.

For a seller, the practical steps are simple. Pull the flood zone for your parcel before you talk price, find out whether you carry flood insurance, and gather any elevation certificate or repair records.

sections.h2: How do Manhattan's tornado and temperature swings affect a house?
sections.html:
Manhattan has a humid continental climate, so roofs, siding and heating systems all work for their living. Average precipitation is 35.77 inches a year, and the temperature reaches 90 degrees or higher on about 59 days a year and 0 degrees or lower on about four days. Snowfall averages 17.6 inches.

The most destructive tornado on record hit at about 10:30 p.m. on June 11, 2008. The EF4 storm destroyed 31 homes and caused about $20 million in damage on the Kansas State campus. An earlier tornado on June 8, 1966 injured at least 65 people.

Manhattan also sits near the Nemaha Ridge, and the strongest earthquake to originate in Kansas, a magnitude 5.1 event, was centered here in 1867. It caused largely minor damage. The Army Corps of Engineers later finished a project in 2010 that replaced sand under the Tuttle Creek dam with more than 350 concrete walls.

sections.h2: What does Manhattan require of owners who rent out a house?
sections.html:
The city has a rental registration program, and the program page says owners must register all rental units. Inspections are not mandatory under that program, but the Risk Reduction office, reachable at 785-587-4506, encourages owners to ask for one and offers a property maintenance checklist.

If your house has been a rental, confirm it is registered before you sell so the question does not come up mid-deal.

  • Confirm that every rental unit you own is registered with the city.
  • Keep leases, deposit records and any inspection results together for the buyer.
  • Call Risk Reduction if you are unsure whether a unit needs attention before a sale.

sections.h2: When are Manhattan property taxes due, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
Riley County bills real estate taxes in arrears. The first half is due by December 20 and the second half by May 10 of the following year, and for 2025 the December payment had to be received or postmarked by Monday, December 22, 2025 because the 20th fell on a weekend. The Treasurer's Office is at 110 Courthouse Plaza in Manhattan, and payments can also be made by phone at 785-377-5385.

Kansas runs the assessment calendar statewide. County appraisers mail valuation notices by March 1, taxpayers have 30 days from the mailing date to start an equalization appeal, and informal meetings with the appraiser run through May 15. If you sell mid-year, the tax bill for the year you are leaving is still coming, so ask the closing agent how the proration will be handled.

sections.h2: What deed paperwork does a Manhattan sale involve?
sections.html:
Kansas requires a real estate sales validation questionnaire with almost every deed that is recorded. Under K.S.A. 79-1437c, a deed cannot be recorded by the register of deeds unless the questionnaire is attached, and the office keeps it for five years before destroying it.

Some transfers are exempt, including gifts, sheriff's deeds and transfers by an executor under court order, and the exemption number must be written on the document itself. Title companies normally prepare this paperwork, so a seller mostly needs to confirm the price and the names on the deed are correct.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale compare with a listing in Manhattan?
sections.html:
A listing gives you the widest audience and the longest process: preparation, showings, buyer financing and the appraisal. A cash sale to a company like ours cuts out the lender, so the closing date is set by you and the title work rather than by a loan file.

If your Manhattan house needs a roof, has water damage, carries tenants or came through an estate, price the as-is route next to a listing. Call or text and we will review the address and explain our number.

faqs.q: Is Manhattan, KS in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it are. The city's own floodplain management plan describes flood risk along the Big Blue and Kansas Rivers, and the Manhattan Levee System protects areas of the city. Whether a specific parcel is in a mapped flood zone depends on its address, so check the parcel with the city before you set a price.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Riley County?
faqs.a: The first half is due by December 20 and the second half by May 10 of the following year, according to the Riley County Treasurer. When December 20 falls on a weekend, the postmark deadline moves, as it did to December 22 in 2025.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental house in Manhattan before I sell it?
faqs.a: The city requires owners to register rental units, and inspections are not part of that program. If the house has been a rental, confirm it is registered so a buyer or title agent does not raise it later.

faqs.q: What is the sales validation questionnaire?
faqs.a: It is a Kansas form that must accompany a deed when it is recorded, unless the transfer is exempt. It records the sale price and conditions for the state's valuation system, and the register of deeds keeps it for five years.

faqs.q: Can I sell a damaged Manhattan house as it is?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners with storm damage, flood damage or deferred repairs can sell without fixing the house first. The trade-off is that an as-is sale is priced for the work the buyer will take on, so compare it with what repairs and a listing would cost you.

faqs.q: How fast can a Manhattan cash sale close?
faqs.a: The timeline depends on title work and on when you want to move, not on a lender. We will give you an estimate after we review the house and the paperwork, and you can choose a closing date that fits your move.
